calls.reason: The only evidence is CoreWeave's Q3 company-wide net loss. One company's result says nothing about whether most Nvidia buyers were unprofitable from their chips.
The forecast's deadline (Nov 19) is after the evaluation date. Reports of about six-times oversubscription cut against it, but pricing and allocation had not happened yet.

There is a real AI-stock selloff and a reported cut to Nvidia's OpenAI guarantee, but J.P. Morgan calls financing-driven industry effects too soon to tell. Shockwaves from the financing shift are not shown.

Anthropic's net losses come mostly from fair-value changes on its notes, and its adjusted results are positive. Menlo data shows spending concentrating in the leading labs. The evidence on the moat and its causal link to profits is mixed.
This is an open-ended claim about Nvidia's growth. The ACCA piece explains the mechanism but shows no case of customer losses actually cutting Nvidia's purchases or growth.
